- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows sharp upward spikes followed by rapid declines, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below prior high.  
- When sentiment is positive but forecast is trending down, reverse the direction — if sentiment > 0.2, avoid downward drift unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive negative sentiment.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 3–5% below forecast, apply a 3–5% downward bias to next forecast unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more), reduce forecast volatility — smooth out sharp swings by 1–2% per step.  
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by > 5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–8% to avoid “overcorrection lag.”
